fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns HfNbTiVAl10 and tensile/fracture modeling, whereas the target study concerns composition screening and experimental validation of Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 against equimolar NbMoTaVW.

It replaces the target intervention—rule-of-mixtures modulus validation, VEC/density screening of 38,326 compositions, and arc-melted alloy fabrication—with an unreported synchrotron/physics-informed-ML workflow.
It specifies tensile testing and crack-tip imaging rather than the demonstrated room-temperature quasi-static compression tests on as-cast specimens.
The proposed micro-strain and secondary-phase mechanism is unsupported and conflicts with the target's single-phase BCC structure and VEC-mediated dislocation-mobility rationale.
The claimed 15–25% accuracy improvement and order-of-magnitude speedup are not supported by the cited evidence.
None of the decisive target outcomes—35.7% compressive fracture strain, 1115 MPa yield strength, 2550 MPa compressive strength, or the modulus-model validation results—are reconstructed.
explanation: There is only broad alignment with predicting mechanical properties of refractory high-entropy alloys. The material, design intervention, loading mode, structural mediator, mechanism, baseline, and outcomes all diverge from the target. The cited papers provide generic support for HEA machine learning or deformation behavior, but they do not establish in situ synchrotron descriptors, physics-informed surrogate performance, or the numerical accuracy and efficiency gains asserted here. The withheld-data experiment and quantitative failure thresholds make the proposal somewhat testable, although validation data drawn from the same experimental series are not strongly independent and the accuracy comparison requires clearly defined experimental ground truth. Thus, the proposal is a potentially testable alternative research idea, but it is unsupported as an account of the hidden study.
